meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: No specific legal instrument was enacted in Portugal with a view to implementing this Directive, as previous legislation was deemed to cover it. In fact, the vast majority of the norms of this Directive seems to have sufficient backing in previously existing legislation. The very few exceptions are cases where the ‘implementation problem’ originates in the Directive 2013/48/EU, to which the Directive (EU) 2016/1919 is closely related.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning the right to legal aid for:
items.comment:
The close relation between the Directive 2013/48/EU and the Directive (EU) 2016/1919 is immediately clear in Articles 1 and 2 of the Directive (EU) 2016/1919, on subject matter and scope: the same provisions and considerations expounded in relation to Articles 1 and 2 of the Directive 2013/48 apply here, since national provisions on legal aid apply to persons who are entitled to a lawyer. In any event, the main legal instruments of relevance for the Directive on legal aid are:

- the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July), which implements Directive 2002/8/EC, of 27 January 2003, to improve access to justice in cross-border disputes by establishing minimum common rules relating to legal aid for such disputes; and

- the Ordinance no. 10/2008, which concretises the provisions of the above Law.

items.text: (a)suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings; and
items.comment: See the comment above.

items.text: (b)persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (requested persons).
items.comment:
See the comment above.

Although the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July) does not explicitly apply to EAW proceedings, and although the LEAW does not call for the application of that legal instrument either (in contrast with the CCP, which, as noted elsewhere, applies in a subsidiary manner to EAW proceedings based on provisions contained in the LEAW), it is unquestionable that the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July) should be construed as being applicable to EAW proceedings.

This is the position that has been upheld in a Report by the Commission of the Portuguese Parliament on Constitutional Issues, Rights and Guarantees, concerning the proposal which would result in the Directive 2013/48/UE (Ofício n.º 30/XII/1ª – CACDLG/2014, sobre a Proposta relativa ao apoio judiciário (COM(2013) 824 final, in www.parlamento.pt), p. 11-12.

But see further below, Article 5 of this Directive.

items.text: 2. This Directive complements Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800. Nothing in this Directive shall be interpreted as limiting the rights provided for in those Directives.
items.comment: See the comment above.

items.heading: Article 2
items.comment: Again, the provisions and comments attached to Article 2 of the Directive 2013/48, on the right of access to a lawyer et al., apply squarely here, since both Directives have the same scope of application, and the Portuguese provisions on legal aid apply to persons who are entitled to a lawyer, in the terms mentioned in the provisions and comments to Directive 2013/48.

items.heading: Article 3

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn:
(1) The system of access to the law and to the courts is aimed at ensuring that nobody be dissuaded or prevented, based on social or cultural condition or on insufficiency of economic means, the knowledge, exercise or defence of their rights.

(2) In order to concretise the above objectives, actions and systematic mechanisms of legal information and legal protection will be developed.

(1) Access to the law and to the courts is a responsibility of the State, to be promoted through, among other, mechanisms of cooperation with the institutions that represent forensic professions.

(2) Access to the law encompasses legal information and legal protection.
The system of access to the law and to the courts shall function in such a way as to ensure that the services provided to its beneficiaries be qualified and effective.
Legal protection [mentioned in Article 2 (2)] encompasses the modalities of legal consultation and legal aid.

items.comment:
The Portuguese system of access to the law and to the courts encompasses:

a) legal information; and

b) legal protection.

In turn, legal protection encompasses:

a) legal consultation; and

b) legal aid.

The latter is the modality which related more closely to the scope of this Directive.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.

nationalActs.title: Constituição da República Portuguesa (Decreto de 10 de Abril de 1976)
nationalActs.titleEn: Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (Decree of 10 April 1976)

provisions.textEn:
(1) Everyone is guaranteed access to the law and the courts in order to defend his/her legally protected rights and interests, and justice may not be denied to anyone due to lack of sufficient financial means.

(2) Subject to the terms of the law, everyone has the right to legal information and advice, to legal counsel and to be accompanied by a lawyer before any authority.

Accused persons have the right to choose an attorney and to be assisted by him/her in any procedural act. The law shall specify the cases and phases of procedure in which the assistance of a lawyer is mandatory.

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn:
(...)

(3) If the defendant does not appoint a lawyer, he/she must, in the moment when he/she is subject to a Statement of Identity and Residence, provide a declaration on his/her income, property and permanent expenditure of his/her household.

(4) The secretary of the court shall assess the economic insufficiency of the defendant based on that declaration and the criteria defined in this Law.

(5) If the secretary concludes that there is economic insufficiency, the defendant must be appointed a lawyer (...).

(6) The appointment of a lawyer in the terms prescribed in the previous paragraph is provisional and depends on the granting of legal aid by the social security services.

(...)

provisions.comment: The "the following Article" mentioned in Article 8 (1) is Article 8-A, which will be addressed throughout this Directive.
provisions.textEn: A person is deemed to be in a situation of economic insufficiency when he/she lacks the conditions which are objectively necessary to fully support the costs of a procedure, in the terms defined in the following Article.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: The latter is the provision which enshrines the abovementioned postulate that the State will bear the costs of legal assistance, regardless of financial hardship, if the defendant chose to be assisted by a lawyer appointed by the State and is ultimately acquitted.
provisions.textEn: [When the defendant did not appoint a lawyer and it is necessary to appoint a lawyer to him/her,] the defendant is informed, in the bill of prosecution, that, should he/she be convicted, he/she will be obliged to pay the costs of the lawyer that has been appointed to him/her, unless he/she is granted legal aid.

items.comment:
In addition to the definitions already provided above, it is important to note that in Portugal legal aid may be provided by the State even if the person is not in a situation of economic insufficiency. The legal framework on legal aid engrains two fundamental ideas: (i) on the one hand, that the State should bear the costs of legal assistance not only when the defendant is in a situation of financial hardship, but also when, regardless of hardship, the defendant chose to be assisted by a lawyer appointed to him/her by the State and ultimately comes to be acquitted; (ii) on the other hand, a defendant who seeks this support without being eligible shall be penalised for such a behaviour.

That said, the fundamental provisions in relation to this Article of the Directive are the following.

items.text: 2. Member States may apply a means test, a merits test, or both to determine whether legal aid is to be granted in accordance with paragraph 1.

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: The latter is the provision which enshrines the abovementioned postulate that the State will bear the costs of legal assistance, regardless of financial hardship, if the defendant chose to be assisted by a lawyer appointed by the State and is ultimately acquitted.
provisions.textEn: [When the defendant did not appoint a lawyer and it is necessary to appoint a lawyer to him/her,] the defendant is informed, in the bill of prosecution, that, should he/she be convicted, he/she will be obliged to pay for the services of the lawyer that has been appointed to him/her, unless he/she is granted legal aid.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.

(4) The secretary of the court shall assess the economic insufficiency of the defendant based on that declaration and the criteria defined in this Law.

(5) If the secretary concludes that there is economic insufficiency, the defendant must be appointed a lawyer (...).

A person is in a situation of economic insufficiency when he/she lacks the conditions which are objectively necessary to fully support the costs of a procedure, in the terms defined in the following Article.

provisions.comment:
Article 8-B of the same legal instrument then regulates the means through which the situation of economic insufficiency may be proved.

Moreover, as an Annex to this legal instrument, a formula is provided for calculating the income.
provisions.textEn:
(1) For the purposes of this law, the assessment of economic insufficiency of a person is made taking into account the average monthly income of that person and his/her household (...).

(2) The objective conditions on the basis of which said assessment is performed are considered by reference to the index of social support [‘indexante dos apoios sociais’]

(…).

(6) If the person or a member of his/her household has amounts deposited in a bank account, or assets liable to negotiation in regulated markets, and their value is 24 times higher than the value of the mentioned index of social support, the person is deemed not to be in a situation of economic insufficiency, regardless of the income [mentioned in paragraph (1)].

(7) Exceptionally and for justified reasons, as well in the case of a dispute with one or more of the members of his/her household, the assessment of economic insufficiency takes into account only his/her average monthly income, alone or together with that of some of the members of his/her household, as long as he/she so requests.

(8) If, in a given case, the highest official of the social security services competent for deciding on the granting of legal aid considers that the application of the above criteria leads to a situation of blatant denial of access to the law and to the courts, he/she may, by reasoned order issued by him/herself, take a decision other than that which would follow from the application of said criteria.

items.comment: Paragraph (4) leaves open the option whether or not to make the granting of legal aid dependent of a merits test, and thus it may be deemed implemented, in spite of the fact that the conditions mentioned in such a provision do not have any equivalent in the Portuguese legal system.

items.text: (a)where a suspect or an accused person is brought before a competent court or judge in order to decide on detention at any stage of the proceedings within the scope of this Directive; and
items.comment: See the previous comment.

items.text: (b)during detention.
items.comment: See the comment above.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that legal aid is granted without undue delay, and at the latest before questioning by the police, by another law enforcement authority or by a judicial authority, or before the investigative or evidence-gathering acts referred to in point (c) of Article 2(1) are carried out.
items.comment: Regarding paragraph (5), the comments made on Articles 1 and 2 of the Directive apply: when the person has the right to be appointed a lawyer or it is mandatory to appoint him/her a lawyer, then this will trigger the right to legal aid, and the national provisions indicated in relation to Article 4 (1) to (4) of the Directive will then apply accordingly.

items.text: 6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn: Legal aid is granted regardless of the procedural position of the person and regardless of the fact that the opposite party to the dispute has been granted legal aid.

items.comment: Portuguese law entitles to legal aid persons other than defendants, so this provision may be considered implemented. See the provision below.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings
items.comment:
As stated above, in comment to Article 1 (1) (b) of this Directive, although the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July) does not explicitly apply to EAW proceedings, it is an established understanding that it does apply to EAW proceedings, a position which has been explicitly upheld by the Commission of the Portuguese Parliament on Constitutional Issues, Rights and Guarantees.

However, this provision of the Directive can be considered only partially implemented, as expounded below.

See also the Directive on the right to a lawyer, which provides for the cases in which the person sought pursuant to an EAW either has the right to be assisted by a lawyer or the appointment of a lawyer is indeed mandatory.

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

nationalActs.title: Regime Jurídico do Mandado de Detenção Europeu (Lei n.º 65/2003, de 23 de Agosto)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on the European Arrest Warrant (Law no. 65/2003, of 23 August)

provisions.textEn: The arrest of a person [pursuant to an EAW] abides by the same requirements provided for in the CCP for the arrest of suspects.
The person arrested [pursuant to an EAW] has the right to be assisted by a lawyer.

provisions.comment: See the relevant provisions of the CCP in the Directive on presumption of innocence and in the Directive on the right to a lawyer.
provisions.textEn: Articles 57 to 67 of the CCP [on the formal designation of a person as a defendant (arguido), the rights and duties springing from this status, etc.] apply as appropriate, and the person sought on account of a EAW, when arrested, should be provided with a document informing him/her of the rights mentioned in the previous paragraphs.
The Code of Criminal Procedure applies in a subsidiary manner to the procedure of execution of an EAW.

items.text: 2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.
items.comment:
Paragraph (2) is fully implemented: (i) When Portugal is the executing Member State, the rules on access to a lawyer and on legal aid apply, albeit not explicitly. (ii) When Portugal is the issuing Member State, a criminal procedure has necessarily already been initiated in Portugal, which in turns means that the person is necessarily and explicitly entitled to legal representation and legal aid as a defendant in this criminal procedure.

However, Article 10 of Directive 2013/48/EU has only been partially implemented: (i) As for Article 10 (4), there is no explicit provision imposing on Portuguese authorities, as executing authorities, a duty to, without undue delay after deprivation of liberty, inform requested persons that they have the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State. This might be achieved through an extensive interpretation of Article 61 (1) (e) and (h) of the CCP, applicable to EAW proceedings ex vi Articles 17 (4) and 34 of the LEAW, but this is by no means certain. If a lawyer is appointed in the issuing Member State, then his/her role will naturally include assistance to the lawyer in the executing Member State by providing that lawyer with information and advice, but there is no explicit provision on this either. (ii) As for Article 10 (5), no implementation at all has been made of this provision.

items.text: 3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.
items.comment: It is: see the provisions and comments to Article 4 (3) above.

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Decisions regarding the granting of legal aid

items.text: 1. Decisions on whether or not to grant legal aid and on the assignment of lawyers shall be made, without undue delay, by a competent authority. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the competent authority takes its decisions diligently, respecting the rights of the defence.

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn:
(1) The decision on the request for legal protection shall be taken in 30 days, counted continuously, including during judicial holidays (…).

(2) Upon expiry of the above deadline without a decision having been issued, the request should be considered as tacitly granted.

(...)

Once the judicial review [of an administrative decision not to grant legal protection] has been received by the court, it is immediately distributed to the judge who is to conduct the review, and this judge shall, through a concisely reasoned order, decide whether or not to grant the legal protection, based on extemporaneity or manifest invalidity.

items.text: 2. Member States shall take necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons are informed in writing if their request for legal aid is refused in full or in part.

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn: The final decision on the request for legal protection is notified to the person who made the request and, if the request involved the appointment of a lawyer, such a decision should also be notified to the Bar Association.

Once the judicial review [of an administrative decision not to grant legal protection] has been received by the court, it is immediately distributed to the judge who is to conduct the review, and this judge shall, through a concisely reasoned order, decide whether or not to grant the legal protection, based on extemporaneity or manifest invalidity.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Quality of legal aid services and training

items.text: 1. Member States shall take necessary measures, including with regard to funding, to ensure that:
items.comment: Article 7 of the Directive contains several provisions concerned with the quality of legal aid services and training. The following national provisions address those issues, especially in the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts. These provisions allow for the conclusion that Portuguese law complies with Article 7 of the Directive, on quality of legal aid services and training. Nevertheless, the enforcement of this provision depends on the amount of funding that is made available by the Government, each year, to the system of access to the law and to the courts. And the widespread perception, at present, is that not enough funding is provided, such that this system tends to ensure legal protection only to individuals who clearly cannot bear the costs of their involvement in a criminal procedure. Thus, there is a number of individuals who face significant economic difficulties but are not entitled to legal aid.

items.text: (a)there is an effective legal aid system that is of an adequate quality; and

nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn: The system of access to the law and to the courts shall function in such a way as to ensure that the services provided to its beneficiaries be qualified and effective.

The costs emerging from this law which are to be spent by the social security services are paid by the State Budget, by transferring the corresponding amount to the budget of the social security services.

provisions.comment: This provision is further concretised by Article 3 of Ordinance no. 10/2008, regulating the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts.
provisions.textEn: The appointment of a lawyer to the defendant in order for him/her to be subject to the first judicial interrogation when arrested, to be tried under highly summary proceedings or for other urgent procedural acts provided for in the Code of Criminal procedure is regulated in Article 39 of this Law, and a list of lawyers and intern lawyers must be organised to stay on call to that effect (...).
The selection of forensic professionals shall ensure the quality of the services provided to those who are granted legal protection within the system of access to the law.
If the same fact gives rise to several proceedings, the system shall ensure that, preferably, the same lawyer is appointed to the person for all those proceedings.

nationalActs.titleEn: Ordinance no. 10/2008, regulating the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts

provisions.textEn: The selection [of forensic professionals] shall strive for ensuring the quality of the services provided to those who are granted legal protection within the system of access to the law.

items.text: (b)legal aid services are of a quality adequate to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, with due respect for the independence of the legal profession.

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn:
(...)

(2) The State guarantees adequate compensation to the forensic professionals who participate in the system of access to the law and to the courts.

(3) Forensic professionals who provide services in the system of access to the law and to the courts may not earn, in the context of their participation in this system, remuneration other than that to which they are entitled based on the present law and on the Ordinance mentioned in Article 45 (2) [i.e., Ordinance no. 10/2008, regulating the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts].
The forensic professionals who do not comply with the rules governing the exercise of legal representation may be excluded from the system of access to the law.

nationalActs.title: Portaria n.º 10/2008, que Regulamenta a Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais
nationalActs.titleEn: Ordinance no. 10/2008, regulating the Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts

provisions.textEn: [T]he appointment of a lawyer is carried out by the Bar Association, and it may be fully automatic, through an electronic system managed by this entity.

items.comment: In addition to the provisions mentioned in the previous item (a), the following should be deemed to contribute to the fairness of proceedings and to the independence of the legal professional as exercises within the context of the system of access to the law and to the courts.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that adequate training is provided to staff involved in the decision-making on legal aid in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings.
items.comment: Since the administrative decision is taken by the social security services, and since these services have specialised qualification to deal with issues of this nature, we would deem this provision as also implemented.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of adequate training to lawyers providing legal aid services.
items.comment:
as indicated above, the appointment of lawyers to participate in the system of access to the law and to the courts is a responsibility of the Bar Association, which may be deemed to be particularly aware of the challenges involved in providing legal aid and protection.

On the other hand, the Bar Association provides training concerning several challenges in the exercise of the profession of lawyer. As far as was possible to ascertain, no specific training exists for the specific challenges of providing lawyer services within a public system of access to the law and to the courts, but the Bar Association does provide wide information on this system, its particularities and possible difficulties [notably in a document named “Elucidário do Acesso ao Direito” (which may be roughly translated as “Understanding the System of Access to the Law”], of December 2015, in https://www.oa.pt/upl/%7B5774e842-8b45-498c-8a9e-297c133fe678%7D.pdf, last accessed 31 December 2020].

items.text: 4. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have the right, upon their request, to have the lawyer providing legal aid services assigned to them replaced, where the specific circumstances so justify.

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn: The beneficiary of legal aid may, in any proceedings, request in a reasoned manner the Bar Association to replace the lawyer that has been appointed to him/her.

The appointment of a lawyer to the defendant [pursuant to the system of access to the law and to the courts] is preceded by information to the defendant that he/she has the right to appoint a lawyer of his/her choice [but at his/her own expense].

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 8

nationalActs.title: Lei do Acesso ao Direito e aos Tribunais (Lei n.º 34/2004, de 29 de julho)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on Access to the Law and to the Courts (Law no. 34/2004, of 29 July)

provisions.textEn: The decision on the granting of legal protection may not be appealed to a superior of the administrative entity that takes such a decision, but it can be appealed before a court, in the terms prescribed in Articles 27 and 28.

(1) The judicial review can be lodged directly by the interested person (…) within 15 days of the notification of the administrative decision not to grant legal protection.

(2) The request for judicial review must be written, but not necessarily in articles; only documental evidence is admitted, and this evidence may be requested by the court.

(3) Once the request for judicial review is received, the social security service has 10 days to revoke the decision to deny legal protection or, if it decides to maintain the decision, to submit it, together with an authenticated copy of the administrative file, to the competent court.

(1) The court competent for the judicial review is that of the legal district of the social security service that ruled on the request for legal protection or, if the request was lodged already during the course of judicial proceedings, of the court before which it is pending.

(…)

(4) Once the judicial review has been received by the court, it is immediately distributed to the judge who is to conduct the review, and this judge shall, through a concisely reasoned order, decide whether or not to grant the legal protection, based on extemporaneity or manifest invalidity.

(5) The decision mentioned in the previous paragraph cannot be appealed.

If an [administrative] decision not to grant legal protection is to be issued, the person at issue must be given the possibility to present his/her claim, in writing, before the decision is actually taken (…).

items.comment:
The provisions and comments attached to 10 of Directive 2016/343 on presumption of innocence apply here.

The following provisions should moreover be taken into account.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account in the implementation of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn: Assistance by an attorney is mandatory: (...) In any procedural act, save for the formal designation of the person as a defendant, whenever the person is blind, deaf, speechless, illiterate, unfamiliar with the Portuguese language, a person under 21 years old, ou the question has been raised whether he/she may be unimputable [owing to a mental disorder] or not completely imputable.

items.comment: There is no explicit provision in the Portuguese legal system equivalent to this provision of the Directive, but Article 64 (1) (d) CCP, already addressed, establishes that it is mandatory to appoint a lawyer to certain persons who are vulnerable, and this, in turn, will trigger the several provisions on legal aid mentioned throughout this Directive.
